Create New Business

The New Business workflow guides you through the setup of a business in RMS, from its core information and liability structure to the operative documents that define the placement. Each step builds on the previous one to create a complete and properly structured business record.

§

Before you start: make sure you have identified the key information and elements needed to complete the Business setup. The specific requirements for each stage and its related documents will be outlined in the following sections as you progress through the workflow.

Businesses → Create

1. Business Details

The Business Details section is the starting point of the workflow, where the general characteristics and key information of the Business are defined. This information must be completed and saved before continuing with the remaining steps. Once the Business record has been created, the Liability Structures and Operative Documents sections become available, allowing you to proceed with steps 2 and 3 and complete the Business setup.

From Businesses → List, click + New Business, top right.

After completing the previous step, the Create Business form will open, allowing you to begin entering the information required to set up the new Business. The form is organized into sections that will guide you through the information required to complete the Business Details.

The following sections provide detailed guidance on how to complete each part of the Create Business form, including the information required for each field and any relevant considerations for its proper completion.

General Details
FieldStatusNotes
ReinsurerRequired*Select the reinsurer to which the new Business will be assigned. The selected reinsurer is also used to identify the Business and generate its Business Code.
IndexindexAutoDisplays the sequential number automatically assigned to the Business by the system. This value is generated automatically and does not require any user input.
Business Codebusiness_codeAutoDisplays the unique code assigned to the Business. The code is automatically generated when the Business is created and is used to identify the Business throughout RMS.
DescriptionRequired*Enter a brief description that clearly identifies the Business and provides users with a general understanding of the risk or operation being registered.
Business TypeRequired*Select whether the Business corresponds to Own business or Third Party business, according to the origin and ownership of the risk being registered.
PurposeRequired*Select the purpose of the Business according to its classification as Traditional or Strategic.
Treatyparent_idOptionalSelect the applicable Treaty when the new Business is associated with or operates under an existing treaty. Leave this field blank when no Treaty relationship applies.
Renewed FromOptionalSelect the previous Business record when the new Business corresponds to a renewal. This creates a reference between the current Business and the preceding period.
Original IDsource_codeOptionalEnter the original or legacy identifier of the Business when applicable. This field can be used to preserve the reference assigned to the Business in a previous system or source.
＋
Business Code is assembled automatically as {year}-{reinsurer acronym}{reinsurer LSK, 3 digits}-{sequence, 3 digits} the moment you save — for example 2026-TOB014-001. You never type it.

The Contract Attributes section defines the key characteristics of the reinsurance contract. Some fields are pre-populated with default values; review each one and adjust the selection as needed to accurately reflect the terms of the Business.

Once all the required information has been completed and reviewed, click the Create button to save the new Business and establish its initial structure.

✓
Once the Business has been created, RMS automatically assigns its Business Code. To continue with the next steps of the setup process, return to the Businesses list and locate the Business you want to continue working on. Click the three-dot menu (⋮) at the far right of its row to display the available actions, and then select Edit. When the Business is opened for editing, the Liability Structures and Operative Documents sections will become available, allowing you to complete the remaining steps of the Business setup.

Business Lifecycle and Approval Process

The platform uses Lifecycle Status and Approval Cycle to provide a clear view of each Business throughout its operational process. While the Lifecycle Status reflects the current stage of the Business based on the coverage periods of its associated Operative Documents, the Approval Cycle indicates its current position within the review and authorization process. Together, these mechanisms provide users with a consistent way to track both the operational status and approval progress of each Business. The following sections explain how each of these processes works and how their statuses change over time.

Lifecycle Status

Definition

Lifecycle Status gives a real-time, automated view of where a Business stands within its coverage lifecycle — from inception through expiration or cancellation. In reinsurance and contract administration platforms, this kind of operational visibility is a core capability: it lets underwriters and management identify which contracts are active, which are approaching renewal or expiration, and which have already lapsed, without relying on manual date-tracking across spreadsheets. Because it is derived automatically rather than entered by hand, it also removes a common source of reporting error, keeping portfolio-level views of the in-force book accurate and current at any point in time.

Once a Business is created, RMS automatically assigns it a Lifecycle Status of On Hold. The Lifecycle Status is not set manually; instead, it is automatically determined based on the Operative Documents associated with the Business. It is updated whenever an Operative Document is created, edited, deleted, or restored. In addition, a daily process reviews all Businesses at 2:00 AM to ensure that any status changes resulting from the passage of time are applied automatically, even when no changes have been made to their Operative Documents.

Lifecycle Status
StatusMeaning
On HoldNo Operative Document has been registered yet, or the next one hasn't reached its inception date.
In ForceAn Operative Document is currently active, and its expiration date is more than 30 days away.
To ExpireAn Operative Document is currently active, but its expiration date falls within the next 30 days.
ExpiredEvery Operative Document on the Business has lapsed, and none of them is a Cancellation.
CancelledThe most recent Operative Document is a Cancellation, and its inception date has already been reached.

Lifecycle Status is read-only everywhere in the form — there is no button that sets it directly. It simply reflects whatever is currently true in the Operative Documents tab.

Approval Cycle

Definition

The Approval Cycle establishes a formal review and authorization step before a Business record is considered final. Segregating the person who creates a record from the person who authorizes it is a standard governance control in reinsurance and contract administration systems, where accuracy and accountability across the underwriting portfolio carry real financial and compliance weight. By requiring a manager's sign-off before a Business is approved, the platform builds an auditable trail of who submitted, reviewed, and authorized each contract — supporting internal controls and reducing the risk of unreviewed changes reaching the active portfolio.

Separately from Lifecycle Status, every Business also carries an Approval Status that tracks whether the record itself has been reviewed and signed off by the creator's manager. The two are entirely independent — a Business can already be In Force while its Approval Status is still Draft or Pending Review.

Approval Status
StatusMeaning
DraftDefault status. The Business hasn't been submitted for review yet.
Pending ReviewSubmitted — waiting on the creator's manager to approve it or request changes.
ApprovedThe manager signed off on the Business as submitted.
Needs RevisionThe manager requested changes. The revision notes are shown to the creator on the record.
Review actions
ActionWhoNotes
Submit for ReviewThe Business's creatorAvailable from Draft or Needs Revision. Notifies the creator's manager.
ApproveThe creator's direct managerAvailable only while Pending Review. Notifies the creator.
Request RevisionThe creator's direct managerAvailable only while Pending Review. Requires written notes, which are shown to the creator.
＋
Every Monday at 8:00 AM, managers with anything still Pending Review also receive a reminder digest email — so a request never quietly falls through the cracks between manager and creator.
Business → Liability Structures

2. Liability Structures

Definition

Liability Structures define the coverage framework applicable to a Business by capturing key elements such as coverage type, country, limits, sublimits, and deductibles. In addition to establishing the scope and financial boundaries of the coverage, this structured information provides a consistent basis for portfolio analysis, enabling the evaluation of exposures, geographic and coverage concentrations, limit and deductible distributions, and other risk indicators across the Business portfolio.

Once the Business is opened through the Edit action, navigate to the Liability Structures tab to begin configuring its coverage structure. To add the first record, click + New Liability Structure. A new window will open where the corresponding liability details and scope can be entered.

New Liability Structure opens a form for one coverage/country pair. Repeat it for every coverage the business carries.

Liability Details
FieldStatusNotes
CoverageRequired*Select the coverage type this Liability Structure defines, based on the entries maintained in the Coverage catalog.
CountryRequired*Select the country associated with this coverage. Only countries within the Region selected for the Business are available.
CSLclsYes / NoIndicate whether this coverage applies as a Combined Single Limit (CSL), meaning the Limit is shared across all coverages rather than applied individually to each one.
Liability Scope
FieldStatusNotes
Limit + DescriptionRequired*Enter the limit amount for this coverage, along with a description that explains what the limit covers.
Sublimit + DescriptionOptionalEnter the sublimit amount and its description when a portion of the coverage carries its own limit. Leave blank when no sublimit applies.
Deductible + DescriptionOptionalEnter the deductible that applies to this coverage, either as an amount or as a number of waiting days, along with a description. Leave blank when no deductible applies.
＋
Every coverage you add here becomes a choice in Operative Documents → Insured Members. A coverage with no Liability Structure can't be assigned a premium later — set this tab up before you start entering insureds.

Business → Operative Documents

3. Operative Documents

Definition

Operative Documents represent the contractual instruments through which a Business is established and subsequently modified over time, including the original Slip and any related Endorsements. Each document captures its own coverage period and relevant operational and financial information, providing a structured record of the terms applicable at each stage of the Business. Together, these documents form the contractual history of the Business and provide the basis for tracking coverage validity, placement arrangements, insured members, premiums, and other information required for its ongoing administration.

Each Operative Document is organized into three sections that capture the information required for its setup: Document Details, Placement Schemes, and Insured Members. Together, these sections define the document's contractual information, reinsurance placement structure, and the insured entities covered under it.

Document Details→ Placement Schemes→ Insured Members
A

Document Details

The document's identity, dates, and its own PDF.

FieldStatusNotes
Id DocumentAutoDisplays the unique identifier automatically assigned to the Operative Document by the system. This value is generated automatically and does not require user input.
DescriptionRequired*Enter a brief description that identifies the Operative Document and summarizes its purpose or scope.
Document TypeRequired*Identifies the type of Operative Document being created. The first document registered for a Business is automatically set to Slip; subsequent documents are registered as Endorsements.
Underwriting Monthrep_dateRequired*Select the underwriting month associated with the Operative Document. This field defaults to the current month when the document is created and can be changed if required.
Exchange rateroe_fsRequired*Enter the exchange rate applicable to the Operative Document. When the Business currency is USD, this field is automatically set to 1.00 and cannot be modified.
Service Feeaf_mfRequired*Enter the service fee applicable to the Operative Document. If no service fee applies, the field defaults to 0.00.
Coverage Period (From / To)Required*Select the start and end dates that define the coverage period of the Operative Document. The total number of coverage days is calculated automatically based on the selected dates. These dates are also used by RMS to determine the applicable Lifecycle Status of the Business.
Filedocument_pathOptionalUpload the PDF file corresponding to the Operative Document. The file is stored privately and automatically named using the Document ID.
!
Document Type is sequenced: the first document on a Business is always the Slip, and the field locks to it — you can't pick anything else, and you can't create a second Slip once one exists. Every document after that is an Endorsement.
B

Placement Schemes

Definition

Placement Schemes define the cost structure that applies to an Operative Document. Each Placement Scheme is based on a Cost Scheme, which is composed of one or more Cost Nodes representing the different costs, commissions, fees, or other components involved in the Business. By assigning one or more Placement Schemes to an Operative Document, RMS identifies which cost structures are available for the premium associated with that document and its Insured Members.

Each Operative Document must be associated with at least one Placement Scheme. Select an existing Cost Scheme or use the Add Placement Scheme option to create a new one directly from the form. Multiple schemes can be associated with the same Operative Document when different placement structures are required.

Search for an existing scheme, or open Add placement scheme → + to define a new one inline without leaving the form. You can attach more than one scheme to a single document.

＋
The Placement Schemes selected in this section determine which schemes will be available when configuring Insured Members. If a scheme is removed, any Insured Member previously associated with it will have that selection cleared automatically, preventing references to a scheme that is no longer applicable to the document.
C

Insured Members

The premium, per insured company and per coverage — this is where the Annual Gross Reinsurance Premium actually gets recorded.

FieldStatusNotes
CompanyRequired*Select the insured company from the Company catalog.
Placement schemeRequired*Select the Placement Scheme through which this insured's premium is placed. Only schemes selected in the Placement Schemes tab are available.
CoverageRequired*Select the coverage that applies to this insured. Only coverages already registered in Liability Structures are available.
PremiumRequired*Enter the Annual Gross Reinsurance Premium for this Company and Coverage combination.

Add one row per insured company per coverage — a company on three coverages needs three rows.

!
Endorsement B — No Premium Change: if the Document Type is Endorsement B, Premium is set to 0 and locked while creating, by design — that endorsement type exists specifically to record a change with no premium impact.
